title: Learning music: printing shop, alto horn and the band's first Eastern tour
summary: With no musical family, White worked in the printing department until about fourteen, then joined the orphanage band on alto horn under Eugene Michael.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Can you remember the music when you were young? Did you play anything or other members of the family?

No members of my family played anything because the fact of it is I was away from my family then. I just considered myself having no family. I knew my sister was at home and I knew Peter was at home with my father in King Street, but the two smaller children, they were dead. And Geneva, she died when I was about 16. She died at around 14. She was kind of chubby and fat and took pneumonia and died. Well, I went back to her funeral. Mr. Jenkins sent me back. I was already a member of the band then also. See, in the printing department, they kept me in the printing department until I, oh I guess I was around about 14 before they even allowed me to touch an instrument. I was a kind of a sickly child. Always coughing, always having had a cold. And they had a doctor who would come there, but he said I had guitar, hay people. So they would avoid putting me in the band, but I wanted to learn music because I could sing. I was a very good singer. So the first season they took me to with the band East. Took me East with the band. You started right on in the carnet? No. Alto Horn. Alto Horn. And the band was taught that season by Eugene Michael. And then, oh, after one season through the East. And these seasons in the East took in everything we would say from, well, Massachusetts straight on down through Pennsylvania, back into Washington, where the Mason and Dixon line ends. Then we'd head for home for school.
